text:
Anya: quick heads-up — I need to jump to the airport in ~15m, leaving warm handoff here. Primary: Mike R., Secondary: Sofia L. I'm leaving a short runbook + what I've done so far. If anything pages while I'm offline, follow the escalation rules below.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT · INC-3421 · inference-hosts cluster · spike in 5xx (503) errors · triggered at 2024-07-12T18:02:10Z · severity: P1

Anya: timeline/context: about 18:00 UTC we saw a sudden 503 rate increase on the inference pool serving hosted-api-prod. Most traffic to models with long context. Impact: ~30% error rate for 2+ customers, increased tail latency. I've cycled the bad ASG nodes once and rolled a config to increase request timeouts to 45s (temporary).

Mike R.: on it. I'll take primary. Can you paste the exact alert query and the logs you pulled?

Anya: alert rule: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\",code=~\"5..\"}[1m])) by (cluster) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\"}[1m])) by (cluster) > 0.15`
logs I pulled (tail):
```
2024-07-12T17:58:09Z inference-12 error: backend timeout kv-cache miss
2024-07-12T17:58:11Z inference-9 warn: queued request dropped, queue_length=256
2024-07-12T17:59:42Z inference-15 error: model load OOM during quantized path
```
I've attached the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-503 (runbook section: "Immediate mitigation")

Devon (infra): FYI the autoscaler autoscaled down aggressively earlier due to wrong cpu metrics — I've bumped min nodes to 4 in the ASG and disabled scale-in for 10m. Also seeing noisy eviction events on one AZ.

Sofia L.: taking secondary. I'll monitor logs and customer reports. If you need me to take primary, ping me.

Mike R.: immediate plan: 1) confirm whether KV cache backend is overloaded 2) temporarily divert low-priority traffic to model-backup pool 3) if error rate still >20% after 10m, escalate per paging rules. I'm going to run `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --selector=pool=hosting` and then `grpcurl` into a couple nodes to reproduce.

Mike R.: running quick check: `kubectl top nodes` shows node inference-az3-2 at 98% mem, others healthy. There are 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff across inference-15.

Anya: notes on previous mitigations I ran: restarted kv-cache service on inference-9, warmed prefixes for high-volume customers, and increased request timeout. I avoided full rollback since that was noisy.

Sofia L.: monitoring customer-impact slack channel. Two customers reported timeouts but not data loss. Marking customer-impact as moderate.

Mike R.: paging/escalation rules (copying from oncall policy):
- P1 (service-wide SLO breach or >25% customer-facing failure for 5+ min): page Primary mobile immediately, then PagerDuty schedule if no ack in 3m. If Primary ack < 15m but unable to mitigate, escalate to SRE Lead (page + phone).
- If incident affects legal/regulatory flows or high-visibility customer: page Eng Manager and CSM at once.
- For infrastructure-level issues (AZ outage, host OOM affecting multiple pools): page Infra Lead right away.
- All pages should include summary, `incident id`, and immediate mitigation steps taken.

Mike R.: executing diversion to backup pool now (`route: low-priority -> hosting-backup`) — pushed config. Will watch error rate for 5m.

oncall-bot: CONFIG CHANGE DETECTED by Mike R. · change_id cfg-9921 · rolling update to route low-priority traffic · started at 2024-07-12T18:12:05Z

Sofia L.: after diversion error rate dropped to ~12% at 18:15 UTC. Latency still high for long-context requests.

Devon (infra): Suggestion: if kv-cache is root cause, we can enable prefix caching on dedicated cache nodes and increase connection pool. I'll draft the exact command: `redis-cli -h kv-cache.internal CONFIG SET maxclients 16000` and we can `kubectl scale deployment/kv-cache --replicas=4 -n infra`. Approve?

Mike R.: approve. Do the scale + config. Also let's add a temporary rate-limit on long-context requests — config snippet: `policies.rate_limit[\"/v1/generate\"] = { concurrency: 8, window_ms: 10000 }`

Anya: nits for whoever picks this up after me: 1) check `/metrics/kv_cache_miss` 2) verify quantization fallback didn't OOM for those specific models (model id: rwd-llama-13b-q4) 3) run smoke tests after changes: `make smoke-inference`

Sofia L.: notes: I'll stand primary if Mike needs to hand off. If we see customer impact again >25% for 5m, I'll escalate to Infra Lead and page Eng Manager per policy.

Mike R.: small follow-ups: updated incident title to include affected models, added customer list to incident doc, and left a checklist (restart, scale, divert, patch).

Anya: thanks team. I'm going to set my OOO flag but will be reachable if PD pages me. Leaving this as the formal warm-handoff: primary=Mike R., secondary=Sofia L., oncall window covered until 2024-07-13T02:00Z UTC. If anything changes escalate as above. :thumbsup:

Sofia L.: ok, marking handoff complete. added note in calendar and pinned runbook in thread.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE · INC-3421 · status: mitigation in progress · last_update: 2024-07-12T18:18:00Z"
